description: Declarative two-axis mode registry for the sk-code parent hub. Every packet is a modes[] entry carrying the discriminator (workflowMode/packetKind/backendKind) plus its advisorRouting contract. The WORKFLOW axis (sk-code-quality/sk-code-review) is process; the SURFACE axis (sk-code-ci/sk-code-skilled) is read-only domain evidence. Implement/debug/verify phase doctrine is consolidated in shared/references/workflow-*.md, symlinked into the surface. The advisor routes the single identity sk-code; the hub resolves the workflow mode and bundles surface packets as evidence.

discriminator.workflowMode: Public hub/mode key. Stable identity used by the hub router and this registry. Carried by every mode.
discriminator.packetKind: The axis discriminator: 'workflow' for process modes that act, 'surface' for read-only domain-evidence packets bundled alongside a workflow mode.
discriminator.backendKind: Which backend runs the mode: surface-router for surface-aware code workflows, review-cache for review output caching, evidence-base for read-only surface packets.

advisorRoutingContract.routingClass: How the advisor finds the mode. For sk-code every mode is 'metadata' = resolved by hub membership; the advisor routes the single identity sk-code and the hub picks the mode. Surface packets are advisor-invisible and reached only by hub bundling.
advisorRoutingContract.packetSkillName: The packet's SKILL.md name. Folder equals packetSkillName for every mode.
advisorRoutingContract.grandfatheredFolderMismatch: false for every mode because folder equals packetSkillName.

surface-axis.description: Declares the SURFACE axis. packetKind:'surface' entries are read-only domain-evidence packets (backendKind:'evidence-base', routingClass:'metadata', mutatesWorkspace:false) bundled alongside a workflow mode via routerPolicy.outcomes.surfaceBundle. They bundle stack knowledge plus the workflow doctrine as read-only evidence; the acting agent applies it — the surface never executes the process itself.
surface-axis.surfaceDetection: A surface entry may carry a surfaceDetection block: label (the detected surface name), role ('specific' or 'fallback'), and pathMarkers, fileMarkers and contentMarkers. A skill outside the hub whose graph-metadata.json names family 'sk-code' can declare the same block as surface_detection, and it is always specific. Detection tries every specific surface first, hub entries in modes[] order and then outside skills by skill_id, then the single fallback, then UNKNOWN. When a specific surface and the fallback both match, the specific surface leads and the fallback comes along as second evidence. The fallback is the hub's own code, so its path markers count only when the resolved real path lands inside the hub's own .skilled/ directory. A surface reached from request vocabulary alone, such as sk-code-ci, declares no block. The registry compiler rejects a hub that does not declare exactly one fallback or that does not rank it last in routerPolicy.tieBreak.

toolSurface.writeScopeNote: Write is scoped to the ephemeral review cache in the reviewing user's cache directory (${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/sk-code-review/<repo-ref>.jsonl), outside the reviewed repository; sk-code-review never writes tracked project files (Edit is forbidden), so the tracked workspace is not mutated.
